tool.name: disassembler walker
tool.description: reconstruct coding haplotypes from Logan unitigs
tool.command:
## Worst-case resident memory is (4 queued + fetch workers + compute workers) ## compressed payloads of up to --max-size-mb each. Compute workers follow the ## job's slots; fetch workers are trimmed so that bound fits in GALAXY_MEMORY_MB ## when the job runner sets it. workers=\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} && fetch_workers=\$workers && if [ -n "\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-}" ]; then fit=\$(( GALAXY_MEMORY_MB / \${DISASSEMBLER_WALKER_MAX_SIZE_MB} - 4 - workers )); if [ "\$fit" -lt "\$fetch_workers" ]; then fetch_workers=\$fit; fi; if [ "\$fetch_workers" -lt 1 ]; then fetch_workers=1; fi; fi &&
## The walker names the reference after its file stem (summary file, multi-anchor ## haplotype tags), so it is linked (or decompressed, for fasta.gz) under the ## dataset name instead of Galaxy's dataset_<uuid>.dat. The regex strips a trailing ## .gz too so a reference_name derived from foo.fasta.gz is just foo, not foo.fasta. #import re #set $reference_name = re.sub(r'\.(fasta|fas|fa|fna)(\.gz)?$', '', re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', str($query.element_identifier))) #if $query.is_of_type('fasta.gz'): gunzip -c '$query' > '${reference_name}.fasta' && #else: ln -s '$query' '${reference_name}.fasta' && #end if
logan-walker #if $input.mode == 'accession': --accession '$input.accession' #else: --accession-list '$input.accession_list' #end if --query '${reference_name}.fasta' --out-dir walker_out --out-fasta reconstructed.fasta ## Scratch dir for shard payloads. The CLI default, /dev/shm/logan-walker, is ## shared by every job on the node and is only 64 MB inside a default Docker ## container, so we point it at the job's working directory instead. --scratch-dir walker_scratch --workers "\$workers" --fetch-workers "\$fetch_workers" --max-size-mb "\${DISASSEMBLER_WALKER_MAX_SIZE_MB}" --min-cov $min_cov --prune-frac $prune_frac $prefer_majority $allow_empty --k $anchoring.k --hops $anchoring.hops --min-shared-kmers $anchoring.min_shared_kmers --primary-metric $anchoring.primary_metric --min-abund $variants.min_abund --min-vaf $variants.min_vaf --min-abund-frac $variants.min_abund_frac --alt-max-detour $variants.alt_max_detour --max-alt-indel $variants.max_alt_indel $variants.no_indel_alts $variants.allow_frameshift_alts $output_options.emit_alts $output_options.emit_vcf $output_options.emit_snv_table &&
## The summary is named after the reference file. mv walker_out/*_walker_summary.json walker_summary.json

param.label: Accession list
param.help: One SRA run accession per line, for example an output of disassembler harvest or stratify. Running the tool over a collection of lists spreads the accessions across jobs (see the help below).

validator.message: Letters, digits, underscores and hyphens only

param.label: Reference CDS
param.help: In-frame coding sequence of the target gene, optionally gzip-compressed. A FASTA with more than one record switches on multi-anchor mode: every record contributes anchors, and each accession's primary haplotype comes from the reference that aligns best.

param.label: Minimum reference coverage
param.help: Fraction of the reference a reconstruction must cover to be reported.

param.label: Pruning depth fraction
param.help: Unitigs below this fraction of the gene's depth are dropped and the path is realigned, which removes the aligner's pull toward the reference. 0 disables pruning.

param.label: Prefer the majority allele
param.help: At two-allele sites, put the more abundant allele on the primary haplotype. When off, the primary keeps the allele that matches the reference.

param.label: Succeed even if nothing is reconstructed
param.help: By default the job fails when no accession reconstructs, so an empty result is not mistaken for a good one. Turn this on when an empty result is acceptable, for example when running over many single-accession lists.

param.label: Hop radius for subgraph expansion
param.help: How far from the anchored unitigs the local graph is grown.

param.label: Minimum shared k-mers for an anchor
param.help: k-mers a unitig must share with the reference to anchor the subgraph.

param.label: Primary haplotype selection (multi-anchor mode)
param.help: How the winning reference is chosen when the reference FASTA has more than one record. Ignored for a single reference.

param.label: Minimum k-mer abundance for a variant
param.help: Minimum ka:f (mean k-mer abundance) of an alternative branch.

param.label: Minimum abundance as a fraction of gene depth
param.help: Raises the abundance floor to this fraction of the median ka:f on the walked path. 0 disables it.

param.label: Maximum detour length (unitigs)
param.help: How many unitigs an alternative allele may traverse before it must rejoin the main route.

param.label: Substitution alleles only
param.help: Refuse any alternative allele that changes the sequence length.

param.label: Allow frameshifting indel alleles
param.help: Also accept indel alleles whose length change is not a multiple of 3. These shift the reading frame.

param.label: Largest indel allele (nt)
param.help: Larger length changes are treated as a rerouting, not an indel allele.

param.label: Output intra-host SNVs as VCF
param.help: One VCF per accession that has at least one recovered SNV, in reference coordinates.

param.label: Output an intra-host SNV table
param.help: One long table of every intra-host SNV across the run, one row per accession, site and allele.

tool.help:
@HELP_SUITE@
-----
What it does ************
Reconstructs the coding haplotype of a target gene in each SRA run, directly from that run's `Logan <https://github.com/IndexThePlanet/Logan>`_ unitigs. For every accession the walker:
1. streams the run's compressed unitigs from the public Logan S3 bucket, 2. anchors unitigs to the reference CDS with shared k-mers and grows a local subgraph around them, 3. aligns the reference to that subgraph with GraphAligner and walks the best path, 4. prunes low-depth unitigs and realigns, removing the aligner's pull toward the reference, 5. recovers intra-host alternative alleles at forks along the walked path.
The result is one primary haplotype per accession in reference coordinates, plus optional alternative haplotypes and intra-host SNV calls.
The walker downloads data during the job, so the Galaxy server needs outbound network access to ``logan-pub.s3.amazonaws.com``.
-----
Inputs ******
- **Accessions**: either a single SRA run accession, or a dataset with one accession per line (for example from **disassembler harvest** or **disassembler stratify**). - **Reference CDS**: the in-frame coding sequence of the target gene. More than one record switches on multi-anchor mode.
-----
Spreading accessions across jobs ********************************
The tool accepts an accession list, so the same tool supports three ways of running a cohort:
- **One job for the whole list.** Simplest, but one job holds the whole cohort. - **One job per accession.** Split the list with **Split file** (one line per file) and run the walker over the resulting collection. Each accession gets its own job, retry and provenance. This stops scaling at roughly 10,000 accessions, where scheduler overhead dominates. - **One job per shard.** Split the list into files of N lines and run over that collection. This scales past 100,000 accessions.
When running one job per accession, consider **Succeed even if nothing is reconstructed**, or filter failed datasets before collapsing the reconstructions into one FASTA for **disassembler msa**.
-----
Outputs *******
- **Reconstructed haplotypes**: one primary haplotype per accession that reconstructed. Headers carry coverage, identity, subgraph size and depth. - **Alternative haplotypes** (optional): intra-host alternative haplotypes. - **Intra-host SNVs (VCF)** (optional): a collection with one VCF per accession that has at least one recovered SNV. - **Intra-host SNV table** (optional): every intra-host SNV in one long table, one row per accession, site and allele. This is the output that scales to large cohorts. - **Bubbles**: the fork structure found along each walked path. - **Summary**: per-accession status, timings and errors.
Threads and memory are set from the job's resources. GraphAligner always runs single-threaded, because its output is not reproducible with more than one thread.
